title: Deduction of tax at source on payment of a certain sum for purchase of goods

effectivePeriod.sunsetNotes: In force from 1 April 2026 as statutory successor to Section 194Q of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

plainTextSummary: Under Section 393(1) Table 8 Item (ii) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (effective 1 April 2026), any buyer whose total sales, gross receipts, or turnover from business exceeds ₹10 Crore in the preceding financial year, responsible for paying any sum to a resident seller for purchase of goods exceeding ₹50 Lakhs in the current financial year, must deduct 0.1% TDS on the amount exceeding ₹50 Lakhs at the time of credit to seller account or payment, whichever is earlier. Penalty rate under Section 397(2) Proviso is 5% if PAN is not furnished or is inoperative.

keyStatutoryThresholds.taxableBaseScope: Tax is deductible strictly on the excess over ₹50 Lakhs, NOT on the aggregate gross turnover.

requiredDocumentChecklist: Valid Permanent Account Number (PAN) of Seller (Checked against Income Tax Portal)
Audited Financial Statements confirming Buyer gross turnover exceeded ₹10 Crore in preceding FY
Cumulative Purchase Ledger for current FY establishing date threshold of ₹50 Lakhs was crossed
Payment / Credit vouchers cross-referencing advance challans
Tax invoice with GST separately stated (to ensure tax is withheld strictly on basic value)
